title: Defining The Keys of The Kingdom Part 2
paragraphs: I believe that you are beginning to understand how and why it is important that we get to know this good news of the kingdom of God. I started with an illustration this morning. That illustration was about a key you found in the house, but no longer knew which lock it belonged to. So, in the end, you had a useless key. I think everyone who has ever had a few keys has experienced that, right? I just looked at it again before I left home; There was a key in my car, and I still ca n't remember what that key is for.

So I possess the key, but the key is useless to me. That illustration is striking because it describes what happens to religious people. Religious people have keys. It is in this book. This is a lot of keys. But having keys and knowing how to use them, or knowing what they are for, is another story. Having the Scriptures but not knowing how they work to unlock the riches God has in store for us is just as bad as having no key at all.

Someone said to me: "He who does not read is no better off than he who cannot read." The same applies to someone who has a key: he is no better off than someone who has no key if he does not know what the key is for. And so the religious leaders in the time of Jesus had the same problem. Christ said specifically to them: "You know the Scriptures." He said: "But you do not know the kingdom of God." That means they had the keys. I would like to briefly summarize where we left off.

We began with a scripture passage that implied and emphasized the importance of the kingdom of God. In the book of Luke, chapter 4, Christ told us why He had come. He says: "I must also proclaim the good news of the kingdom of God in other cities." Why? Because that is the reason why I have come. I think that is an important reminder for tonight. And the emphasis in this section, this verse, lies on discovering the purpose of Jesus' coming to earth. Pay attention to what He Himself says.

He did not really come for Golgotha. He did not come for the resurrection. He did not come to perform miracles. Those were not His goals. Those were means to an end. What was the purpose of His coming? He tells us what it is. To preach the gospel of the kingdom of God. The good kingdom of God. Therefore He came. He says: " His coming was therefore inspired by the surrender of the kingdom to man." The second scripture passage we read is Luke 12:32. And there it says: " Do not be afraid, little flock." Why?

For your Father was happy to give you something? The kingdom. We also read Matthew 25:34, and that is an important passage. I just want to repeat that for those who had to work this morning; Maybe they didn't quite understand it. In this passage, in Matthew 24, verses 25-34, Jesus says: "Come, you are blessed by my Father," He says; "receive your inheritance, which is the kingdom of God." And then He says that that kingdom has been your inheritance since the creation of the world.

That means that the kingdom already existed before the earth. The kingdom was given to you before the earth. And therefore He created the earth. The earth had to be created so that you could carry out the mission of the kingdom. God wanted His kingdom, His rule, to manifest itself on a visible planet. So He first created children in the spirit, gave them the responsibility, and had to create the territory for it. So actually, the earth and the sky were created.

The physical heaven and earth were created so that God could fulfill his kingdom wishes through his children. The reason Christ came was to give us back the inheritance that had always been ours. How long has the kingdom belonged to us? From the creation of the world. That is important. Christ has therefore truly come. Our inheritance is not Golgotha. Our inheritance is not even the resurrection. Golgotha, the resurrection, the blood, and all those things we talk about so often are not the good news.

They are the processes or means to arrive at the good news, namely the kingdom of God. Let's take another look at another verse in Revelation 5:10. Revelation is the last book of the Bible. It therefore forms the culmination of God's entire plan. And in this verse, does God ultimately say that He will make us into something? A kingdom of priests to serve our God. And where shall they serve Him? They will rule on earth. This morning I did not emphasize the word 'rain', because we will come back to that later.

But just remember that, okay? But take a look. He didn't say that we would sing, dance, or clap on earth. He said we were going to do something? Where would we rule? On Earth. So our destination is Earth. Now religious people say that our destination is heaven. No, our ultimate destination is still Earth, because that was the original mission. Let man have something? Dominion over the fish, the birds, the cattle, and over the whole earth. So God created man in his image, and God blessed man and said: " What?

Dominion over the fish, the birds, the cattle, and the earth." In other words, God's original plan was the earth. And his ultimate plan will be the earth. He will get what he has always wanted. Everything between Genesis and Revelation is a program. It is not the main thing. So we see here that his desire is to let us rule and reign on earth again. It is important to note here as well that in the following verse we discuss the law and the prophets.

Luke 16:16 says that the law and the prophets were proclaimed to John. Since that time, since John, the good news of the kingdom has been preached. And that is important, because he says that until John, the kingdom was not emphasized. But after John, that was God's focus. John is therefore the most important prophet in the Bible. Moreover, Jesus said about John: "There is no greater prophet born of men." Why? Every prophet before John spoke about the coming of the Messiah.

Johannes actually spoke about it and introduced him. John was therefore the greatest prophet in the sense that he was the most privileged, because he could not only say that he would come, but could also literally introduce him personally. He further says that when this kingdom is preached, many try to worm their way into it. In other words, people want it when they understand it. When I was in London a few weeks ago, I spoke about this kingdom and briefly explained why people do not come to Christ.

I picked up this subject again when I was visiting Marilyn Hickeyi for a moment a few days ago. We were talking about this in church. I told the congregation that Christ says in the ninth chapter of Matthew that the harvest is ripe. And what does that mean? Abundant. Pay attention, who was he looking at? Humanity. To the crowd. And 2,000 years ago, he said that the harvest was ripe. That means the harvest must be rotten by now. Stinks. Do you know what happens if you store apples or mangoes and don't pick them?

They fall, begin to rot, become mushy, worms emerge, and they start to stink. In other words, the things that taste so good are going to stink. Do you know why? Because the harvest was ripe, but you did not pick it. Christ says that he looked at the crowd. Matthew chapter 9, verse 13. And he saw them as sheep without a shepherd. And what does he say then? He says that they are like sheep without a shepherd. And then he turned to the disciples and said: The harvest is plentiful and ripe.

And that verse ends like this: Therefore do not go to the harvest. Go to the Lord of the harvest. Lord means owner. And ask Him to send out laborers. In other words, do not go to the harvest. Go to the Lord and let Him send you out if He wills. The last sentence says 'His harvest'. Two things here.' He is Lord of the harvest—what does 'what' mean? He is the owner. And 'His harvest' means that He lays claim to it.

That means that every unsaved person on this planet, whether they are Buddhists, Hindus, Muslims, Shintoists, Scientologists, Unitarians, Moon worshippers, it does not matter who they are, Rastafarians or atheists, God has already ripened them. What is so amazing is that he says the harvest is ripe. So he is not trying to let them ripen for you. They are ready to be picked. But what is the problem according to him? I have no workers. In other words, the quality of the people who can reach them is very limited.

Why is this important in light of what we just discussed? He says here that those who understand the kingdom force themselves to do so. People want it if they understand it. That means that if they do not run after something we have, what we have is not what God has commanded us. Do you know what I find incredible? Every time I talk to someone about the kingdom, it doesn't matter what they believed before, they get excited about it. Do you know why? Let me tell you why.

Because the kingdom offers an answer to man's greatest problem. I know what it is. The greatest problem of man, I repeat it once more, is that he cannot control the circumstances. That is your biggest problem. Nothing feels as helpless as when the doctor says: " I can't do anything more for you." How do you feel then? Nothing feels worse than when the banker says: "Your creditworthiness is not good enough. We cannot give you the money." You feel helpless, don't you?

Nothing feels worse than when someone says: " Uh, you didn't get the job. Thanks for your application." I mean, there is that nasty feeling in life when you can't control the circumstances. Well, the kingdom gives you power over circumstances. Let me put it differently. The reason why people pursue religion, regardless of which religion, is because that religion promises them power over circumstances. The most helpless circumstance we know in life is what? Death. We cannot stop them.

So all religions try to give you some kind of explanation of how you can overcome them. But the kingdom of God gives you power not only over the circumstances in this life, but also in the life after death. For Christ is the only one who has proven that it is possible. After all, Buddha never returned. Mohammed never returned. I have respect for Mohammed. I have read the Quran, and 90% of it is the Old Testament. So I at least give him credit for consulting his sources properly. Yes. I have respect for the Hindus.

They have 600 million gods. So one of them must work after all. But not a single Maharaja has ever returned from the dead. So they are still not sure that they can control the circumstances of death. That is why the resurrection is so important to the world, because Christ not only showed that we can overcome poverty, want, and the elements such as the wind and the ocean, but he also showed that he had authority over what? Diseases. He healed people and had authority over demons. He drove them out.

But he also had authority. He says: "And I go to the grave and I come back to show you that I also have power over those circumstances." That is why the kingdom is so important, because the kingdom promises us authority and victory over circumstances. What does it have to do with? Dominion. But our problem is that we do not understand the message. Let us therefore briefly discuss what a kingdom is. A kingdom encompasses...

this list is not complete, but I will mention some basic elements of a kingdom, and that is what Christ preached. First, a kingdom must have a king, a sovereign. Secondly, it must have a territory. In other words, an area over which it has influence and rules. Thirdly, a kingdom must have citizens. Mind you, this kingdom we are talking about has been misunderstood and turned into a religion. Jesus hated religion. His greatest opponents were religious leaders, and he stuck to them as the only ones he appealed to.

You surely still remember that Jesus never addressed a sinner, but rather religious leaders, because religion reduces citizens to members of religious organizations. Yes. A kingdom has no members. Churches have members. Ecclesiastical religious groups. They are just like Rotary clubs, Key Clubs, and church clubs. We are all just a bunch of clubs. We become members and as a result, we do not experience the reality of life in the kingdom, because we are religious members.

My main goal for the next two years is to transform you from religious Christians into citizens of the kingdom. For if I manage to accomplish that, you will bear the responsibility to take the circumstances into your own hands. A kingdom has citizens. By the way, the difference between a citizen and a religious person is that a citizen is a legal entity. It is a legal entity. They have rights. A religious person has emotions. They are trying to appease their god. So they make sacrifices.

They, you know, the heathens are religious people. And you, oh dear, that's a good one. I just felt that. The heathens are religious people. So if you study Hinduism, Buddhism, Shintoism, or any other -isms, you will see that those people constantly offer things to their gods, such as food, money, or fruit. They even cook food for their gods and place it under small dishes, and when the rats eat of it, they say that God ate it. I mean, it is incredible. If you study these religions, you see that this happens.

Why do they offer those things to those gods? They tell you why. Because we do not want God to be angry with us, or because they want God to protect us. In other words: if I do this for you, you do that for me. If I do this for you, you see, there is a kind of reconciliation politics going on. So, if a hurricane comes, or a tidal wave, or if someone is struck by lightning, they say: "The gods are angry." You see, now they are scared. Oh, God, we have done nothing to please that God. That is religion.

Well, is Christianity different then? If you give 10 dollars, you get 100 back. You see, we have still ended up in that politics of reconciliation. Let me tell you something. In a kingdom, you do not appease the government. If you are a citizen, there is no question of giving in. So what is actually going on? Rights. Once you are a citizen, you can make demands. Oh, you don't understand me. A government is not there to be served, but to serve the citizen.

Therefore Jesus says: "Come to Me, for I give you rest when you carry a heavy burden." He says: "Cast off all your burdens." In other words, in this kingdom it is the other way around. The government works for you. But in religion, you work for religion. You are not a citizen. It is a very different way of dealing with religion. And fourth, every kingdom has a constitution. It must have a covenant. In our constitution, we naturally call that the Bible. And fifth, every kingdom has laws.

Those laws must be obeyed for a kingdom to function. And everyone must obey the laws. And seventh, every kingdom has a government. That is the prevailing authority. And eighth, what does every kingdom have? Say it out loud. Privileges. Say it again. Privileges. Say it again. Say it again. Citizenship is a privilege. I want to emphasize that. You have no right to be a citizen, but once you are a citizen, you have rights. That is a big difference.

That is why it is so difficult to become a citizen of any country, because citizenship is a privilege and it gives you privileges, and then what? Rights. And that is why citizenship is so important for everyone in the world. An illegal immigrant has no rights and no benefits that he or she can demand from a government. The same applies to the kingdom of God. You know, Christ was in that synagogue that day, remember? And that woman was sitting bent over. She was sick.

And I tell this story often, because it is such a good example of the kingdom. He sat there and the Bible says that he stood up. Now he is about to do something. Everyone knows that. Oh dear. Here we go again. It was the Sabbath. There was a woman who had been sick for years. She sat bent forward. She couldn't even look up. The Bible says that she had a problem. Maybe a hernia, a hernia or something like that, or a tumor or something similar, that made her sick. Who was standing there with Jesus?

The religious leaders. Look, religion makes you comfortable in your discomfort. Religion makes you accept circumstances as the will of God. Well, talk to me. Religion tells you: "Well, it is the will of the Lord that you are this way." You see, religion makes you accept a situation that you can change yourself. So those religious people said to Jesus, or rather, they said it to each other first: "What is he going to do now?" They started talking about themselves: "Oh, it is the Sabbath.

He shouldn't be healing on the Sabbath." And then Jesus heard them. So he began to talk, and he shifted his focus from their religious talk to thoughts about the Kingdom. He said, and I believe he might even have said it without looking at him: "Is this woman a daughter of Abraham?" Where was he going now? He went to contract. Yes. Where did he go? To law. Look, as a religious person, she is a member of the church. But as someone who serves God's kingdom, she is entitled to healing. Amen.

So they wanted her tithes and offerings. Yes. Make sure she keeps coming to church. It does n't matter that much to us whether she gets cured. As long as she sits in her place and pays her tithes. That is religion. Religion gives you no power to overcome circumstances. Now look where Christ is going. Christ does not heal her because he has compassion on her. Religion is based on the idea that God should have mercy on you. As long as I can move God.

If only I can move him with my tears and with how bad I feel, oh God. Oh yes. If only I can make God have mercy on me. Christ said: "Look, I am not going to heal her at all because I have pity on her. Let's talk about rights. Is she not a daughter of Abraham?" Yes. She is a Jew. Good. Have I then not made a covenant with Abraham? Yes. Yes. That none of these diseases will be among you. Is that correct? Yes.

So if I can determine that that disease does not belong among you, then you have the right to be free from it. You know, he didn't ask if the woman was religious or anything like that. Oh dear. I tell you, you do not get things from God. Well, this is going to be difficult. Oh dear. Oh dear. It is difficult to teach us this, you know, because I get into trouble. You do n't have to be saved to receive things from the kingdom. Well, what a surprise, huh? See? See? Okay, you're a bohemian, right? You are a bohemian.

Okay, either you are an American or some of you are from England. Right, British history. Okay. Does it matter now whether you are black or white, red or yellow, or whether you have civil rights? No. Once you are a citizen, it doesn't matter. Suppose you speak Spanish or French, you don't speak the language of the country, you still get things, right? Once you are a citizen, you have rights. What if you are Catholic, Baptist, or Methodist? Do you still have rights as a citizen of your country then? Certainly.

What if you are a Buddhist or a Hindu, or do n't believe in God at all? You have rights in your country too, don't you? Because it does not depend on those other things. As soon as you have contact with the government, you have rights. Let me prove it to you. The person who best understood the Kingdom of God was not even a Jew. That makes my point. He was a pagan centurion, a Roman. But he understood how the kingdom works. This man did not worship Jehovah.

In fact, he had been sent there to oppress the Jews, to keep them in check. He was in command of 6,000 soldiers. Centurion, a mighty man. And his servant was sick. His personal assistant fell ill. And he tolerated Jesus for a while during those Crusades. You know, in the area where he was in charge, came this young man from Galilee, a man in his thirties who held these meetings; And I believe that his soldiers were on duty to ensure that no riots broke out, because it was their job to keep everything under control.

So I believe that the centurion often came by and listened to this young man, to Jesus speaking about the kingdom, and he was fascinated by this man. He observed Jesus too, of course, you know, and probably heard that he was healing people. But now he has a problem. What is wrong with him? What is wrong with him? A circumstance that he cannot control. Do you think he tried everything he could? Yes, he had money. He had power. So he sent a man to doctors, I am sure they lived nearby, and tried all sorts of things.

The man did not get better. So he said: "Let me try this man who taps into a different source." Well, I'm getting excited now. Everyone is in heaven. Look, when the doctors are done with you, you had better have another key that gives you access to a heavenly source of healing. So this heathen centurion thought that this man could heal my servant. He came to Jesus. What did he say? He said: "Lord, uh, my servant is sick."

Before he could finish his sentence, Jesus replied that he found that interesting, because Christ did not normally offer himself voluntarily. But at that moment, even before the man was finished, Jesus offered himself. He said: "My servant is sick at home." Christ said: "I will come and heal him." Then the man said: "You do not need to come. Well, you must delve into that kingdom. It is difficult." The man said: "I understand what you understand. You and I understand each other."

"It is like this: Caesar is in Rome. I am thousands of kilometers away from Rome. I am here in Palestine, in the Middle East. But the headquarters of my kingdom is in Rome, Italy. But I am here in Palestine. And my authority in Italy gave me the same authority in Italy. Yes. So if I tell a soldier to go, he does not hear me. He hears Caesar. Why? Because of my relationship with Caesar. If I tell someone to come, he comes. If I tell someone to go, he goes. Why? Because I am a man who is supposedly under authority.

Look, the key to getting things from the kingdom is that you must submit to his authority. And this pagan man opened a lock. Sir, he used the key. The man put the key of authority in it. He said: 'I know that even now, if you say that you are healed and speak your word like that, ' he says, 'I know that your word will work in the same way as my word.'"" And Jesus answered, listen now, He answered. He said: 'I have never seen anything so great. You are talking about Pharisees, scribes, Herodians.

You are talking about religious people in Judaism.' He said: 'Look, this man has more faith than any Jew I have ever met.' You must study what this man knew. The man simply knew a key to authority. He said: 'You get things done by understanding authority.' And Jesus said: 'Go. Your servant is healed.'"" And the Bible says that when he went home, at the same hour that Christ said that, they told him that the boy had risen. You see, the privileges and rights in a kingdom come from what? Citizenship.

I believe that the centurion followed Jesus after that. There is no doubt about that. Because when you get a reaction like that, it is difficult to walk away and ignore that source of authority. Yes. The next thing is that a kingdom has ethical codes and every kingdom has what? An army. We have already talked a little about that. We can discuss that later in the conference or to come back to in the series. But what is an army? The angels. Uh, the angels. The angels look after the citizens.

One of the important things here is the fact that the citizens in a kingdom do not fight. And that is important, because religion has turned the church into an army. Nowhere in the Bible—I know this is a harsh statement—but nowhere in Scripture is the church ever called an army. But how many books have been written in which the church is the army of the Lord and that we are engaged in battle? Jesus never says it and he never teaches it." In fact, he says that he has ordered his army to protect the civilians.

So the Kingdom of God, if you truly understand it, places you at the head of the army. Who does the army actually fight for? The citizens. Let me ask you a question. And now comes an important question: what do you have to give up when you become a soldier? Your citizenship. Do you realize that you are no longer a civilian when you are a soldier? That is a heavy blow. In other words, I believe that God is saying: "Look, if you religious people don't want to become soldiers, I can't take care of you.

Then take care of yourselves." That is why you fight so much. The angels are so angry with you because you don't let them do their work. So, while you are thinking about it, Daniel had a problem. What do you do when you have a problem and you are a civilian? You pick up the phone and call the police. That is the army. And when you call the police, who calls? The civilian. I think it is amazing how it works. You have the power to pick up the phone if someone violates your rights.

And you can call the army, the police, and they have to come. As a civilian, you have authority over the entire police force. Yes. That is right. That is amazing. They don't just come, but they also put a siren on their car and stop everyone to come. You don't know what I am talking about. When Daniel picked up that phone and said: 'Lord, I have problems here in Persia.'" The angel left it headquarters. On the way, he heard the siren and a traffic jam of demons formed.

The angel signaled back: ' Michael, I have a problem.' Michael C, clear the way. Talk to me, someone. Doctor, Daniel did not fight. Say along with me: Daniel did not fight. Say it again. Hallelujah.' You know that we are all talking about intercession, and we need to study that again. Intercession simply means waiting for the police to come. Woohoo. Daniel, what? Only waited 21 days. Daniel said: 'Listen, I can afford it, because my government does not lie.'

They told me that they would send someone and that if I had to wait 21 days, that man would come. And when the angel appeared, he said: ' Daniel, I have come.' And this is why. Because of your words. Amen.' He said: 'The day you prayed, when the phone call to heaven came, that was exactly the day that the government me released. Tell your neighbor that an angel is on the way. "" Come on, tell your neighbor that an angel is on the way. Tell your neighbor: don't give up. Keep believing in what you have prayed for.

Clap your hands and praise God. That is what prayer is all about. Hallelujah. You know, when you call the police, you do n't have to speak loudly. Hallelujah. Some people pray: "Lord, look, just call. He can even use a mobile phone. Just walk around and see. That is why I am going to write a whole new book about prayer next year, because for people, prayer is one big religious experience." Oh, you can't handle this. Tell your neighbor: I'm going to relax tonight. Let the army solve the problems.

Just let the army solve the problems, man. Don't handle the problems yourself. Christ said: "Cast all your worries on Me, man. Let the angels handle it." When you read the Bible, you see that every situation was handled by angels. Yes. When Joshua arrived and saw Jericho, I thought: I have a problem. The next thing that appeared was a man, an angel. He was wearing what? Military clothing Now you all have to talk to me. Joshua said: "Uh, are you with them or with us?" His answer was interesting.

He said: "I am the captain." The man said: "Look, do you think I look mean? Just look at the men I lead. I'm just the leader of what?" The army. Army, what does that mean? Armies In other words, Jericho is in trouble today. Come on, raise your hands. Praise God. Hallelujah. You get it. Yes, but if you are a religious Christian, this does not work for you, because now you are the army of the Lord. No wonder you take a beating every day. They beat you. The demons are hitting you.

You cannot fight against flesh and blood. Use flesh and blood, man. Citizens have the right to lead the army. Hebrews chapter 1, last verse: "Are angels not ministering spirits, sent out to serve those who have come to salvation? They are here to serve us." Well then, how do you ensure that this kingdom is at work within you? I quote this Scripture because I wanted to show you that Christ thought only of the kingdom.

Before he died, he preached about the kingdom for three and a half years and taught nothing but the kingdom. He went to hell, received the keys, and rose again from the dead. This is after the resurrection. Let us read what is written in verse 2 of Acts 1. It says: "After his suffering," that is to say on Golgotha, "he appeared to these men and gave many convincing proofs of his life." What was that? His resurrection. He appeared to them during what? A period of 40 days.

That means after he was raised from the dead. He was on earth for 40 days and spoke with these men. Read the last sentence. What does it say there? And what did he talk to them about? One subject: the kingdom of God. He did not speak about Golgotha. Not about the blood. Not even about the resurrection. For Golgotha, the blood, and the resurrection were merely means to regain the kingdom. That is why Christianity is such a depressing religion, because we sing a lot, but cannot pay our bills.

It is frustrating to say, "I achieved the victory, I achieved the victory," and then you have nothing when you come home. Something is not right. That's right. Come on. Let's stop fooling ourselves. I am a child of the King, but you cannot pay your mortgage. There is something wrong with those two claims. If your father is a king, you can at least pay off your house. Therefore Jesus said to the disciples, I mean the Pharisees: " Do you know what? You know the Scriptures, but you do not want to enter the kingdom.

I do not let people in." And then he said, oh dear, I'd better not use that, because you won't forgive me. In any case, he said: "Woe." Woe means damned. He cursed them. Who were they? Religious leaders. What did they do? They kept the people out of the kingdom. Intense, isn't it? Look, look what was going through his mind after the resurrection. The ceiling that played in his mind before the resurrection. Amen.

He spent forty days at a seminar in which he taught them the same things he had taught them about the kingdom for three and a half years. Acts chapter 1, the same chapter, a few verses further on. So when they came together, they asked him: "Lord, are you now going to establish and restore the kingdom of Israel?" He said: "Look, you are crazy." His answer was interesting. What did he answer? He said: "Look, you have misunderstood. I am not here to depose Caesar and exterminate Pilate.

I am not here to establish a military kingdom. " They were still thinking of Judas, the Jewish Messiah. For what did the Jews expect? A military leader. Christ said: "No, you are wrong." He said: "Although you have read Isaiah about the Messiah, you have misunderstood the details. The details say that he will become a suffering servant. He will be mutilated, hang on a cross, and be unworthy to look at.

In other words, you are looking for a military leader, and I come as a suffering servant to prepare you to receive the kingdom again." He said to Pilate, you know, when Christ confronted Rome, he confronted Pilate. That was Caesar's representative. And Caesar said to Jesus: "Are you a king?" Jesus said: "Yes, that is me. You know, you say it right. You say it correctly." But then Jesus said: "Let me explain something to you. That was the first time he ever spoke in a courtroom. Okay? And I appreciate that he spoke.

He never spoke with Herod, because Herod was a fool. That man was paranoid. Okay? But when he spoke with Pilate, who was he speaking with? With someone from the kingdom. So he knew that Pilate would understand the language of the kingdom. Pilate asked: 'Are you a king?'" Christ answered: 'Yes, indeed, you are right. You said it. I am a king.' He said: 'Oh, by the way, uh, I just have to let you know that my kingdom is not of this world.'

He said: 'For if my kingdom were of this world, my soldiers would fight for me.' Yes. In other words, if I were to join the army, you would have been my servant and would have said to me: ' Pilot, you are lucky that I am not joining the army, for I could summon ten legions of angels right here and now and destroy you.'"" Do you remember when he was arrested in the garden? Well, this is good. This is a good example. This is a religious person who also puts his faith into practice. Who was that religious person?

Peter, that boy, religious, he loves to fight. Ready to fight. They come to arrest Jesus. Peter says: 'Touch him. Touch me.' Tell your neighbor that you don't have to defend the kingdom. Tell your neighbor, God, no, you cannot defend your own kingdom. How can you defend the kingdom of God if you can't even pay your rent? Peter draws a sword and starts fighting for Jesus. Religious mentality. What did Christ do? Christ says: 'No, Peter, put away your sword. I don't need you to fight for me.'
